### Added
- **Workflows left switched off are now counted.** Pausing one is normal;
  leaving it parked for a year is clutter every admin reads past. The report
  says how many are off, how many nobody has touched in six months, and names
  the longest-abandoned with the date last edited. Costs no extra API calls.
- **Owner rotations that can never assign anyone are now flagged.** HubSpot only
  hands a record to someone holding a Sales or Service seat, so a workflow
  rotating ownership between teams of Core or view-only users fails every time,
  leaving the record with whatever owner it had. The report names the workflow,
  the teams, and why nobody in them is eligible. It reports only what the seat
  rule proves.
- **The collision surface now says when a workflow writes to an associated
  record.** Some actions set a property on the associated contact or company,
  not the record they run on. The property name alone hides that, exactly where
  the report tells you to check before pointing an agent at a field.

### Fixed
- **Stale contacts read as near-zero on every portal.** The signal filtered
  every object on `hs_lastmodifieddate`, which HubSpot leaves empty on virtually
  every *contact*, and an empty value slips straight through a "last modified
  before" filter. Contacts untouched for months counted as fresh, so every
  report so far showed roughly 0% stale contacts: the reassuring answer, and the
  wrong one. Contacts now use `lastmodifieddate`; other objects were always
  correct. On a reference EU1 Enterprise portal the stale share went from 0.7%
  to 8.6%.
- **A hygiene signal that cannot be measured now says so instead of reading
  green.** Before counting stale records, HubScan checks the date property it
  filters on is actually populated. Where it is largely empty the report says
  staleness could not be measured for that object, and why. An unaskable
  question should never look like a clean answer.
- **Names containing a "|" no longer break the tables they appear in.** A team
  called "Automation | SysAdmin" split its row into extra columns: still
  rendered, just misaligned.
